research_question: Among executed end decisions in the historical full-200 run, does Actor end confidence distinguish legal terminal states from illegal terminal states?
hypothesis: H-CALIBRATION-GAP: illegal terminal ends have end-probability/confidence distributions that substantially overlap legal successful ends, implying that Actor end confidence is poorly aligned with the environment's stop-legality predicate.
competing_explanation: H-LOW-CONFIDENCE-END: illegal terminal ends have systematically lower end confidence/margin than legal ends, indicating a sampling/calibration-tail problem rather than high-confidence legality confusion.
reference: EXP-PREMATURE-END-DYNAMICS-001 verified 16/16 historical sub-horizon failures ended with end. It also showed terminal-only p(end) jumps in failures and in 10/11 unique successful controls, weakening the search-triggered-rise interpretation.
repeat_or_treatment: Zero-rollout retrospective audit of existing historical videos only. Primary comparison is all recoverable legal successful terminal-end events versus the 16 confirmed sub-horizon illegal terminal-end events. No policy/environment intervention.
unique_variable: Observed terminal legality label at an executed end: legal successful end versus illegal failed end. This is observational, not manipulated.
fixed_conditions: Use only the aligned historical 2026-08-03 full-200 artifacts
Primary illegal set is the 16 already confirmed eps_len<600 failures with final executed end
Primary legal set is every successful episode with a recoverable terminal video frame; ObjectNav success requires an end action, but video recovery must still validate the probability frame
Use one frozen bar-geometry/action-row mapping for all videos
All probabilities are video-rendered quantized approximations; zero-width bars are below rendering resolution, not exact zero
No simulator, model load, checkpoint load, new episode, replay, Probe, reset treatment, or extra forward
Do not claim clean-B0 prevalence or SafeRL causation from this historical audit
metrics: Recovered legal terminal-end count and illegal terminal-end count
Terminal end margin: p(end) minus largest non-end rendered probability
Preterminal p(end) at t-1 and max over previous five decisions where available
Terminal jump delta p(end) from t-1 to terminal
Action-distribution entropy when all rendered bars are reliably recoverable
AUROC of terminal p(end) and end margin for legal versus illegal terminal events, with episode-level bootstrap confidence intervals
Category/expert_length strata only as secondary descriptive sensitivity checks
expected_result: If legal and illegal terminal confidence strongly overlap, treat the problem as terminal legality discrimination/calibration rather than gradual search-triggered quitting. If illegal ends are consistently lower-confidence, prioritize stochastic sampling/termination calibration.
falsifying_result: H-CALIBRATION-GAP is weakened if legal terminal ends have clearly higher p(end)/margin than illegal ends with stable separation across quantization sensitivity checks.
alternative_explanations: Conditioning on executed end selects for high p(end) in both groups
Legal and illegal groups differ in category, scene geometry, episode length and task difficulty
The historical evaluator provenance is not formal clean B0
Class imbalance (many more legal than illegal ends) affects uncertainty
Actor confidence overlap does not prove target legality information is absent from hidden representations
stop_conditions: Fewer than 14/16 illegal terminal frames are reliably recoverable
Fewer than 150 legal successful terminal frames are reliably recoverable
Action-row/bar geometry cannot be frozen consistently across the corpus
Analysis would require simulator/model execution or hidden-state reconstruction
superseded_reason: Researcher determined that further p(end)-based legal-vs-illegal calibration substantially overlaps already completed termination-probability analyses and has insufficient incremental information value.
